subject: PO gating: sequenced invoices per entity & net-terms carveout
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PO requirements for Redwood - invoicing cadence & net terms

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a few gating items we need to resolve before we can issue a formal PO:

- We require a separate PO and invoice per legal entity (Arcadia North, Arcadia Systems). We cannot accept a single invoice that aggregates multiple entities into one payment.
- Invoices must include the internal project code (Proj: ARC-ENT-23) and the AP reference number.
- Net terms are Net45 by default for our vendors. We can consider Net30 if a prepayment is provided.
- Preferred cadence: invoices issued on the 1st of each month per entity (our ERP posts on the 5th).
- For larger commitments, we evaluate discounts tied to billing cadence / prepay.

Attached is our PO requirements PDF — it lists field-level validations our AP team will enforce. Please confirm whether Redwood can generate per-entity invoices automatically and provide a sample invoice template and evidence you can map to our ERP (EDI/flat-file).

Michael
Michael Torres
Procurement Manager
Arcadia Health Systems

Attachment: Arcadia_PO_requirements.pdf

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements for Redwood - invoicing cadence & net terms

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. High level we can support both patterns you describe, with a couple of implementation options:

Option 1 — Per-entity invoices (preferred from your description): Redwood issues separate PDF invoices per legal entity on the 1st of each month. We can include the project code and AP reference fields you need. This will be the fastest path and keeps your ledgers separate.

Option 2 — Consolidated statement + per-entity invoice detail: Redwood can produce a consolidated monthly statement that aggregates spend, plus a set of per-entity line-item files for your ERP. If your ERP cannot consume the statement as payment input, you still get separate invoice files for posting.

Discount/design notes: we commonly offer two levers for enterprise customers — committed annual spend discounts (tiered) or a prepay discount (smaller, applied if customer prepays). For example, a 10% list discount for a firm annual commitment, or ~2% for a prepay/Net30 concession. 

Can you confirm: (a) whether Arcadia can accept a consolidated statement for visibility while still paying per-entity invoices, or (b) must each legal entity receive and remit against an independent invoice only? Also, do you have a target discount threshold tied to the annual commitment?

I’ve attached our onboarding checklist and a sample invoice export for your AP team to review. If you confirm option 1 is required, I’ll loop finance to finalize concession terms.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_po-onboarding-checklist.docx

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-02T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements for Redwood - invoicing cadence & net terms

Mina — appreciate the options. A couple clarifications from AP:

- We cannot post against a consolidated statement. Each legal entity must receive an individual invoice file (PDF + machine-readable line item CSV) that our ERP ingests. That said, a consolidated visibility statement is fine for our stakeholders, but it cannot replace per-entity invoice files.
- For our procurement committee to approve any discount >5%, we need an assurance of either prepay or a contractual annual commitment (we typically request 12 months confirmed spend).
- If Redwood can deliver per-entity invoices on the 1st and provide a flat-file mapping example (column names, sample CSV) and an implementation timeline (2–4 weeks preferred), procurement will route the PO.

We are open to a 10% discount tied to a 12‑month committed spend, but that must be honored under Net45. Alternatively, a 5% discount with no prepay under Net45 is more likely to be greenlighted quickly. Also include any one-time implementation or mapping fees — our finance team needs to know up front.

Attachment: AP-mapping-requirements.xlsx

—Michael

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: PO requirements for Redwood - invoicing cadence & net terms

Ben / Vanessa — forwarding Arcadia’s AP requirements. Quick summary: they need per-entity invoices (PDF + machine CSV) issued on the 1st, Net45 terms, and are asking about discounts: 10% for a 12‑month commitment, or 5% with no prepay. They explicitly asked for any implementation/mapping fees up front.

Two concession options I recommend we consider:

A) Approve 10% list discount conditional on a signed 12‑month committed spend (deal ARC-8421). Keeping Net45, but require 30% prepay at onboarding (reduces credit exposure).

B) Approve 5% list discount, no prepay, Net45, charge a one-time $5,000 AP mapping/implementation fee to cover engineering/ops work for per-entity invoice export and ERP mapping.

Pros: B gets the deal moving quickly and aligns to our standard credit posture. A gives higher ACV but increases credit/risk. If finance signs off on B I’ll confirm with Arcadia and push the DocuSign amendment for the SOW.

Can you confirm which option we should offer? If neither, please suggest edits.

Thanks,
Mina

Mina / Vanessa — +1 to Option B. Approve the 5% discount under Net45 and require a one-time $5,000 implementation fee to cover AP mapping and testing. No prepay. Rationale: protects cash while keeping the deal simple. Please ensure SOW amendment explicitly states: per-entity PDF + CSV line-item output, delivery cadence (1st of month), and acceptance testing window (10 business days post-delivery).

Subject: Re: PO requirements for Redwood - invoicing cadence & net terms — Decision and next steps

Michael — thanks for the quick turn. Arcadia’s ask is approved with the following commercial terms (final):

- Discount: 5% off list for the contracted period (no prepay).
- Payment terms: Net45.
- Implementation fee: one-time $5,000 for AP mapping and delivery of per-entity CSV exports and invoice schema. Fee payable on SOW signature.
- Delivery: Redwood will provide per-entity PDF invoices and a machine-readable CSV export on the 1st of each month. Acceptance testing window: 10 business days after first delivery.

Next steps: I’ll prepare a short SOW amendment covering the fee and output spec and send via DocuSign for signature. I’ve attached a sample invoice and a link to the DocuSign placeholder. If you can confirm the legal entity names and the exact project code mapping (ARC-ENT-23 + any subcodes), engineering will schedule the mapping work (target 2 weeks).

Links / attachments: redwood-invoice-sample.pdf; https://docusign.com/placeholder/ARC-8421-amendment; https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/arcadia-onboarding

Appreciate it — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Accounts
Redwood Inference
